referenceList.doiPolicy: DOIs appear as full https://doi.org/ URLs at the end of reference entries (all worked examples in the guide carry one).

provenance.claim: mode: “Indicate references by number(s) in square brackets in line in the text … e.g., "as demonstrated [3,6]. Barnaby and Jones [8] obtained a different result"” — square brackets in line, mapped to 'parenthetical-numeric'.
sortOrder: “Number the references in the reference list in the order in which they appear in the text.”
authorTruncation: “for more than 6 authors the first 6 should be listed followed by 'et al.'”. Also: “the shortened form for last page number. e.g., 51-9”.
journalAbbreviation: “Abbreviate journal names according to the List of Title Word Abbreviations (LTWA)” — LTWA is the ISO 4 abbreviation list, mapped to 'iso4'.
collapseRanges: standard Vancouver-numbered convention; the guide's own examples show only comma lists (“[3,6]”), no explicit range statement.
Journal reference style is applied by the publisher at proof stage regardless: “Our journal reference style will be applied to your article after acceptance, at proof stage.”

formats: “Vector drawings: Save as EPS or PDF files embedding the font”; “Color or grayscale photographs (halftones): Save as TIFF, JPG or PNG files using a minimum of 300 dpi”. Tiered floors above 300 dpi for other art: bitmapped line drawings 1000 dpi, combination line/halftone 500 dpi — minDpi records the halftone floor; the tiers are in this note.

widthPresetsMm: derived from the guide's stated pixel minimums at 300 dpi — “single column width: min. 1063 pixels” = 3.54 in ≈ 90 mm; “full page width: 2244 pixels” = 7.48 in ≈ 190 mm. Arithmetic on documented values, not a stated mm figure.

palette: “Please ensure that color images are accessible to all, including those with impaired color vision.” Mapped to 'colorblind-safe-recommended' (imperative phrasing but presented as accessibility guidance, not a rejection criterion). Color is free: “If you submit usable color figures with your accepted article, we will ensure that they appear in color online.”

wordLimit.scope: body text only — excludes abstract, references and title page
body of the letter — excludes figure legends and tables

requiredSections.label: Title page (title, authors, affiliations with lower-case superscript letters, corresponding author)

provenance.claim: Article-type table, quoted: Original Research (includes review articles) “4,000 word limit (not including abstract / references / title page)”, “Structured abstract of up to 250 words”; Letter to the Editor “No Abstract”, “1,000 word body of the letter strict limit (the word limit does not include figure legends or tables)”, “Maximum of 10 references”, “Maximum 1 table or figure (can be multi-panel)”, “No Subheadings”, starts “Dear Editor...”; Editorial “Written by invitation only”, “3,000 word limit, with a mandatory abstract”, “Unstructured abstract is allowed”. Preamble: “word limits include only the body text and do not include the abstract or references”.

Keywords: “You are required to provide 1 to 7 keywords for indexing purposes.” Highlights: “You are required to provide article highlights at submission … 3 to 5 bullet points, each a maximum of 85 characters, including spaces.” CRediT: “Corresponding authors are required to acknowledge co-author contributions using CRediT”. Acknowledgements: “placed in a separate section which appears directly before the reference list”. Competing interests: “All authors must disclose any financial and personal relationships …”. Funding: “Authors must disclose any funding sources …”.

availabilityStatements.data left null: the guide says “you are ENCOURAGED to state the availability of any data at submission” — encouraged, not required; the schema's boolean cannot express that, so the stance is recorded here instead of inventing a value.

submissionFormat: “Format Word files in a single-column layout. Double-column formatting is only permitted for LaTeX submissions.” Double spacing and line numbering are NOT stated anywhere in the guide → null.

Affiliation markers: “Indicate affiliations using a lower-case superscript letter” — note this differs from SUNA's superscript-numeral default; recorded for title-page fidelity, not currently a schema field.

notes: Verified against the live ScienceDirect Guide for Authors on 2026-08-17 (previous version of this profile was a 403-blocked skeleton).
Highlights are REQUIRED at submission: 3-5 bullets, each ≤85 characters including spaces, uploaded as a separate file named with the word 'highlights'.

Reference style is Elsevier Vancouver-numbered: “[1] Van der Geer J, Hanraads JAJ, Lupton RA. The art of writing a scientific article. J Sci Commun 2020;163:51-9. https://doi.org/…” — shortened final page numbers (51-9), >6 authors → first 6 + et al., LTWA journal abbreviations. The publisher reapplies its reference style at proof stage.

figureLabel 'Fig.': the guide's own appendix-numbering format is “Table A.1; Fig. A.1, etc.” — the only in-guide statement of the label form (Elsevier house convention), generalized to main-text figures.
Word files must be single-column; double-column is LaTeX-only.
Clinical trials: registration number in the manuscript, preferably at the end of the abstract; for blinded trials, a section labeled 'Integrity of the Blind' is requested.
Case series/case reports are encouraged to be submitted as Letters to the Editor.
